en.title: Squid Game Producer Leads Asian Producers Alliance Launch in Busan
en.summary: A landmark alliance has been formed by independent producers from five Asian territories at the Busan International Film Festival. Spearheaded by Kim Ji-yeon, producer of the global phenomenon **Squid Game**, the group aims to foster cross-border co-productions and bolster creators' rights.
en.body:
In a move that could redefine the landscape of Asian independent cinema, the Asian Producers Alliance (APA) was officially launched at the Busan International Film Festival's Asian Contents & Film Market. This groundbreaking collaboration brings together independent producers from five distinct Asian territories, united by a shared vision to champion cross-border co-production and strengthen the protection of creators' rights.

At the heart of this historic announcement was **Kim Ji-yeon**, a pivotal producer behind the worldwide sensation **Squid Game** and a board member of the Producers Guild of Korea. She had the honor of reading the alliance's founding declaration, a document outlining the ambitious goals and principles that will guide the APA. This alliance represents a powerful collective voice, ready to tackle the unique challenges and opportunities faced by independent producers across the continent. The formation of the APA underscores a growing demand for greater collaboration and solidarity within the global film community, particularly in fostering diverse storytelling and ensuring fair compensation and creative control for artists.

## A United Front for Asian Storytellers

The establishment of the APA is more than just a new industry body; it’s a testament to the increasing global influence and artistic ambition of Asian cinema. By pooling resources, expertise, and networks, members of the APA aim to facilitate more seamless co-productions, allowing for richer, more diverse narratives that resonate across cultural borders. This initiative is particularly timely, as streaming platforms and international film festivals continue to highlight the immense talent emerging from Asia. The focus on creators' rights is also crucial, promising a more equitable future for those who bring compelling stories to life. The producers involved are not just looking to create content; they are looking to build a sustainable ecosystem that empowers independent voices.

## What's Next for the Alliance

While specific project details have not yet been announced, the APA's formation sets the stage for future collaborations. The alliance is already looking towards potential cross-border AI film projects slated for 2026, with companies like Netflix, No. 13 Panic Pictures, and Mini Productions reportedly attached. Further announcements regarding the alliance's strategic roadmap and initial projects are expected in the coming months, promising an exciting new chapter for Asian independent film.
